name: a BN4 Soul's unison's last frame, the fight's first
why: BN4 unites a Soul as a state of MegaMan's: at the turn's start (0x0800B658) the hand's Soul pseudo-chip becomes his pending form (AI data +0x10), and his family 0x0D (0x080EBA44, BN4_FAMILY_UNITE) plays the unison by its phases, its last on the fight's clock; BN6 crosses before the fight (the crossing's phases, BN6_CROSSING_PHASES at 0x08014A82, run in the battle's phase before the fight's timer counts). So at the frame BN4's MegaMan is in state 0x0D his object, AI data and collision data, his pending form, the unison's effect (its phase 1's 0x080E18EE), the run order and his panel are the unison's; and its three sounds (0x129 its phase 0's, 0x080EBABE; 0x157 its picture's, 0x080E369A; 0x158 its phase 1's, 0x080EBB32), begun before the fight, are said at the frame after it, where BN6's crossing's were begun before the trace
evidence: bn4_soul_thun: BN4's MegaMan in state 0x0D at t1 alone, his ready state 6 from t2; BN6's in his ready state 8 from t1; BN4's sounds 0x129, 0x157 and 0x158 at t2

name: the battle's actors held through BN4's unison
why: BN4's unison stops the battle's time (the battle's flags' bit 4, BN4_TIME_STOP 0x08007948, BN6's twin 0x0800A098), and its actors' runner gives every actor its held routine instead of its state while it is stopped (0x08013D94-0x08013DA8: bl 0x080104DC): on its first held frame, +0x18 0, the routine copies +0x36 to +0x30 and +0x3E to +0x32 and sets +0x18 4 (0x080104DE-0x080104F2); +0x18 goes back to 0 as time runs again, +0x30 and +0x32 keep the copies. BN6's runner and held routine are the same code (BN6 0x0801B4AA, 0x08016BFC, the same bytes), but BN6 crosses before the fight, its time never stopped in the fight's frames, so its actors keep their +0x30 and +0x32 as they began. Read so after BN4's unison: an actor's +0x18 4 at the unison's frame where BN6's is as it began, and its +0x30 to +0x33 BN4's copies of its own +0x36 to +0x39 where BN6's are as they began
evidence: romlab, BN4's state at bn4_soul_thun's first Custom screen and its keys: write 0203b288=3c/2 at 080104e6 lr 08013dad f12912, the frame MegaMan enters state 0x0D (the Mettaur's object 0x0203B258: +0x30 the copy of its +0x36, 0x3C)
bn4_soul_thun: the Mettaur's obj+0x30 BN4 0x3C at every frame, BN6 0; its +0x18 4 at t1 alone; bn4_chip_invis (no Soul): 0 in both

name: the attack's variables' +5 BN4's unison leaves
why: As MegaMan's turn starts with a form pending (0x08013B14: 0x0800B8B0's test), BN4 writes 2 into his attack's variables' +5 (movs r0,#2; movs r1,#0x70; adds r1,r1,r7; strb r0,[r1,#5] at 0x08013B1C-0x08013B22) and sets his state 0x0D, the unison (0x08013B24-0x08013B26: BN4_SET_ACTION, which clears the variables' +0 alone). BN6 crosses by the crossing's phases (BN6_CROSSING_PHASES), which write none of his attack's variables. The byte stays BN4's 2 while his state is his ready one, until his next attack's power attack writes it in both (ThunSoul's 0x58: strb r0,[r7,#5] at 0x0800D2A4); read so from the unison until his first other state
evidence: romlab: write 02035b95=2/1 at 08013b22 (BN4's state at bn4_soul_thun's first Custom screen, its keys, `writes 02035B94 4`)
bn4_soul_thun: ai+0xA5 BN4 2 from t1 to t153, BN6 0; equal from t154, his charged shot

name: his ready state after the unison, BN4's two frames behind
why: After the unison BN4's MegaMan enters his ready state (6) at t2, BN6's (8) before the fight: its first wait (its phase +0x0A 0 until its count +0x20 runs out, its set-up byte +0x0B) runs in both, BN6's two of BN4's fight frames ahead at the spec's lag of 1. Each such field of his object is read against BN4's two frames on, while BN4's wait is not done and his state is the same then; from BN4's phase 4 (t11) both are compared as ever
evidence: bn4_soul_thun: BN4's count 9 at t2 where BN6's at t3 is 7, BN4's 7 at t4; BN4's phase 4 from t11, BN6's from t10

name: a moved Soul's power attack by each game's number
why: A BN4 Soul's loadout names BN4's power attacks (BN4_FORM_LOADOUTS, 0x080184F0, +3 the charged shot's: ThunSoul's 0x58); the move copies each with its family's unit into BN6's grown power attacks and writes BN6's number into its loadout (SOULS_LOADOUTS, past BN5's six rows). src/emu/soulpower.c's tables() lays the grown table out as BN6's own (BN6_POWER_ATTACK_COUNT), BN5's Souls' moved ones (soulcode_bn5.c's powers), their empty ones (empty_powers), their Chaos Unison's (chaos_powers), then BN4's in soulbn4.c's order; tools/xdiff_bn4_souls.py's bn6_power reads the same counts from the sources, so a Soul another track adds before BN4's moves the number in both. His AI data's power attacks (+5 to +8, BN6_AI_POWER_CHIP to BN6_AI_POWER_C) read BN4's number as BN6's so, where BN6's MegaMan holds the move of BN4's form
evidence: soul_thun's expect: loadout ffff00{bn4_power:6}ffff (0xA5 while BN5's Souls' are 8 moved, 3 empty and 6 chaos)
bn4_soul_thun: ai+0x07 BN4 0x58, BN6 0xA5 from t2

name: his NameID in a Soul, BN6's by his form
why: BN6 names MegaMan by his form as he takes it (0x08015B22: BN6_FORM_NAME_BASE 0x1AB + the form, the proxy's 0x1B3 for a Soul, src/emu/bn6_forms.h), the object ids' table giving his arm and records by it; BN4 keeps his one id, 0xA0 (the trace's low byte of NameID, src/dev/xdiff_bn4_trace.c obj_segs), in every form, its code giving a form's look by the NaviStats' form (+0x24) and BN4_STATS_SPRITES instead. Read so while BN6's MegaMan holds the move of BN4's form
evidence: bn4_soul_thun: obj+0x28 BN4 0xA0, BN6 0xB3 at every frame of the united battle

name: the Soul's state, each engine's place
why: BN4 keeps a Soul's turns in MegaMan's AI data (+0x19 its turns, BN4_FORM_TURNS' 3; +0x18 those counted, 0x0800BA20) and its form in the NaviStats (+0x24, written by the unison at 0x080EBB80); BN6's engine keeps them in its Souls block (BN6_SOULS: its Soul, BN6's number of the move, and its turns left, src/emu/soulunite.c, soullife.c), its AI data's +0x18 and +0x19 none of it. The two are held to each other at every frame (xdiff_bn4_souls.py checks: BN6's Soul the move of BN4's form, its turns BN4's +0x19 less +0x18), so BN4's bytes there are read as BN6's block's
evidence: bn4_soul_thun: ai+0x19 BN4 3 from t2, BN6 0; BN6's block Soul 0x0D and turns 3 (player block +0x78, +0x7A)

name: the pending form after the unison, BN6's kept
why: BN4's turn's start writes MegaMan's pending form at each turn: the hand's Soul's, 0 for a form's end, else 0xFF none (0x0800B6D0); BN6's pending record keeps the form taken (BN6_CROSS_PENDING +0, BN6_RECORD_FORM, copied from the Custom screen's record at the turn's start, 0x080147E4) for the battle. So BN4's 0xFF and BN6's proxy form (8) are one state while BN6's MegaMan holds the move of BN4's form
evidence: bn4_soul_thun: pending BN4 0xFF from t2, BN6 8 from t1

name: BN4's timed form's frames, BN6 none
why: As a form is taken BN4 writes its frames (BN4_FORM_FRAMES, 0x08018088, by form: 600 for each Soul, 960 for DarkSoul) into MegaMan's AI data +0x2C (its form's state, 0x0800E05C); its turn's start counts them down for DarkSoul's form alone (0x0800B6A4-0x0800B6B2) and his palette flashes under 90 of them (0x0800BB18), so a Soul's stand unread. BN6 takes no DarkSoul and keeps no such field. The trace lays BN4's +0x2C at BN6's spare (+0xF3, src/dev/xdiff_bn4_trace.c's leftovers); read so where it holds his form's frames and BN6's byte is 0
evidence: bn4_soul_thun: ai+0xF3, +0xF4 BN4 0x58, 0x02 (600) from t2, BN6 0

name: BN4's count of a form's charged shots, BN6 none
why: MegaMan's ready state counts a form's charged shots and rapid busters into his AI data +5, to 5 (0x0800E270-0x0800E288, called at 0x080EEC00 and 0x080EEC34 as it takes the requests 0x20 and 2); its ten bytes (0x0800E27E-0x0800E289) are in neither BN5's ROM nor BN6's (searched whole). The trace lays BN4's +5 at BN6's spare (+0xF0); read so where it is 1 to 5 and BN6's byte 0
evidence: bn4_soul_thun: ai+0xF0 BN4 1 from t154, BN6 0

name: his buster's charge, each engine's places
why: BN4 charges in his AI data with two counters (+0x30 the chip charge's, +0x32 the charged shot's, u16, counted on while held: 0x0800BC1E-0x0800BC34, 0x0800BC40-0x0800BC60), the button (+9: 1 A, 2 B, 0x0800BC3A, 0x0800BC66), a level each (+0x0A, +0x0B: 0 under 10 frames, 1, 3 at the charge time, 0x0800BB50-0x0800BB7A) and the levels kept as B is let go (+0x14, +0x15, 0x0800BE48-0x0800BE4E), and spawns his glow (the fourth kind's 5) once a level is set (0x0800BD9E, its slot AI data +0x58). BN6 keeps one counter (+0x1B, u8, held at the charge time: 0x08012F14-0x08012F24), a level (+0x1D: 0, 1, 2, 0x08012F30), the button (+0x1E, 0x08012EEC, 0x08012F02), its key handler's requests (+0x44's 0x20000 A and 0x40000 B, 0x080130B4-0x08013114, cleared at 0x0801312A) and a glow (the fourth kind's 8) spawned once as he begins (0x080173CE, its slot +0x58). Each byte is read against the other's: BN6's counter BN4's charged shot's held at its charge time (BN4's cache +0x36, the trace's +0xFE), its level BN4's by 0, 1, 3 as 0, 1, 2, its button BN4's (the trace's +0xF2), BN4's chip charge's none; BN6's request bit its button's; BN4's kept levels 0, 1 or 3 where BN6 keeps none; BN4's glow in play where BN6's stands, and his slot for it
evidence: bn4_soul_thun: B held from t60: BN4's +0x32 1 at t62 to 0x5C at t153, BN6's +0x1B 1 at t63 to 0x5A (90) at t152 and held; BN4's level 1 at t71 and 3 at t151, BN6's 1 at t72 and 2 at t152; BN4's glow T4:0x5 in play t71-t153
